test.name: First plan must survey what's already attached to FAN-cluster persons before planning new searches
test.description: q_001 asks why/when Michael Sheahan moved to Schuylkill County. His brother Patrick already has a sourced tree fact -- a 1875 land purchase in Schuylkill County, seven years before Michael's earliest confirmed presence there -- sitting unused. A sound first plan should surface and build on this already-attached FAN-cluster evidence (a sibling arriving years earlier is a classic chain-migration signal), not proceed as if it doesn't exist. Mined from a live alpha-feedback report (issue #1948): the tester asked why plan item 1 didn't check sources already attached to tree people, and the agent's own answer named the gap -- the skill's 'verify the starting point' step checks assumptions, not what's already attached.

judge_context: The tree gives Patrick Sheahan (I2, Michael's brother, linked via I3) an 1875 Residence fact in Schuylkill County whose value is a land purchase (Deed Book 42, p. 118), cited to S1, seven years before Michael's earliest confirmed Schuylkill presence (1882, log_002).

Whether the reply or a new plan item states what Patrick's deed records is decided in code (test_research_plan_states_sibling_purchase fails the run when it is missing). Do not grade it, and do not deduct on any dimension for whether, where, how prominently or in what words Patrick's deed is stated.

The plan should still include new record-type items for Michael's own movement and its cause (land/deed, tax, church/parish, probate, or naturalization, per the localities entry -- civil vital registration doesn't start until 1906, so it's out of scope for this 1870-1882 window) -- surfacing Patrick's fact is additive, not a replacement for planning new searches about Michael himself.

Should NOT plan a new search whose stated goal is to (re)discover Patrick's 1875 land purchase or residence in Schuylkill County -- that fact is already sourced and attached; planning a fresh search for it would show the skill found it by re-searching rather than by surveying the tree it already had. A deed search on Patrick or Michael from 1875 on that cites the deed already held and looks for OTHER transactions (Michael as grantee or witness, Patrick's later sales) is legitimate FAN work, not this failure.
